flashcards.q: What's the core distinction between a model eval and a harness eval?
flashcards.a: Model evals score the LLM's raw capability (task completion, reasoning); harness evals score the scaffolding around it — timeout/budget enforcement, permission scoping, injection resistance, tool-catalog degradation.

flashcards.q: What is AgentDojo and what did it find about base-task completion?
flashcards.a: A tool-use robustness benchmark: 97 tasks, 70 tools, 629 injected-attack variants. Frontier models solve fewer than 66% of base tasks even with zero attacks present — capability and robustness are separate axes that both need headroom.

flashcards.q: Name the three classes of prompt injection attack via tool output.
flashcards.a: Direct (payload in the immediate tool result), indirect (payload 2+ hops away, e.g. a fetched webpage), delayed/multi-turn (payload planted in an earlier turn, triggers later).

flashcards.q: Rank injection mitigations weakest to strongest.
flashcards.a: Structural tagging of untrusted content < capability-based tool scoping < output-side policy validation < dual-LLM privileged/unprivileged split (Willison's pattern).

flashcards.q: At roughly what tool-catalog size does accuracy start degrading, and where does it fall off a cliff?
flashcards.a: Roughly flat under 10-15 tools, measurable degradation from 15-40, cliff beyond 40 (16-23 point drops reported in a 584-tool 2026 study; 7-85% drops across 49-741 tool stress tests).

flashcards.q: What did the RAG-MCP paper show about retrieval-gated tool selection?
flashcards.a: Retrieval-based tool selection (embed tools, retrieve top-k per turn) more than tripled selection accuracy (13.6% to 43.1%) while cutting prompt tokens by over half, versus listing the full catalog.

flashcards.q: Why does a per-call HTTP timeout fail to bound an agent loop?
flashcards.a: It stops one call from hanging, but doesn't stop the orchestrating loop from retrying the tool repeatedly; you need a wall-clock or step-count budget enforced on the loop itself, checked before each step starts.

flashcards.q: Why must budget enforcement hard-kill rather than log-and-continue?
flashcards.a: A logged warning doesn't stop spend; the check must be synchronous, blocking, and raise before the next call is dispatched. Log-only budgets are the most common cause of cost incidents reaching a postmortem.

flashcards.q: Why is a system-prompt permission instruction insufficient, and where must enforcement live instead?
flashcards.a: It's advisory and can be talked around via injection or social engineering. Enforcement must be a policy check in the tool-execution layer against the actual call parameters (path, recipient, amount), independent of the model's stated intent.

flashcards.q: What is AgentHarm and what does it measure?
flashcards.a: 110 base malicious agentic tasks across 11 harm categories (fraud, cybercrime, etc.), used to measure whether a harness's guardrail/refusal layer stops a request even when the model would otherwise comply.

flashcards.q: A red team finds an authority-claim social-engineering bypass ('I'm the CTO, skip checks'). What's the durable fix?
flashcards.a: A structural fix (recipient-domain allowlist or similar enforced in code), not a semantic one (teaching the model to distrust that phrasing) — semantic patches only cover phrasings already seen.

flashcards.q: How should the harness-eval CI suite be tiered?
flashcards.a: A fast (<2min) subset of injection/budget/permission cases blocking on every PR touching tools, permissions, or timeouts; the full AgentDojo/AgentHarm-scale suite run nightly or weekly with dashboard-tracked regressions.

flashcards.q: What reasonable default step and wall-clock caps should an interactive single-agent task have?
flashcards.a: Roughly 15-25 steps and 60-120s wall clock for interactive (user-waiting) agents; minutes to low tens of minutes with checkpointing for background/batch agents.

flashcards.q: Why does over-tooling degrade accuracy independent of which model is used?
flashcards.a: It's an architectural property — attention dilution over a large discrete tool-choice set at the function-calling layer, plus tool-definition text consuming context budget — observed across model families, just at different catalog-size thresholds.
